question: How do I apply for graduation at City Tech?
gold_answer: Check your Degree Audit with an advisor first: you are ready to graduate once you have 60+ credits for an associate degree or 120+ for a bachelor's, a GPA of 2.0 or better, and have completed credits in residency, the Writing Intensive requirement, overall liberal arts and science credits, General Education (Pathways) and major requirements. The page links a PDF, 'Steps to apply for Graduation in CUNYfirst', for how to apply. Apply by the graduation filing date in the Academic Calendar: students who apply late may not have their names in the commencement program and may have their degree awarded at the next conferral date.

gold_answer: The CST Department offers an internship program: a 3-credit course in the BTech degree in Computer Systems. question: How do I view my Form 1098-T in CUNYfirst?
gold_answer: Log in to CUNYfirst at https://home.cunyfirst.cuny.edu, click the Student Center tile, select the Financial Account tile, click View 1098-T in the left sidebar, then select the Tax Year link to open the form. You can download it as a PDF (turn off your pop-up blocker). 'No Data Available' next to a year means you are not eligible for a 1098-T for that year. A 1098-T is not issued if federal grants, scholarships or third-party payments met or exceeded your total tuition charges for the calendar year. A paperless option is available by clicking Grant Consent on the View 1098-T page.

question: If I drop a class after September 3, will it still count toward my financial aid enrollment status, and what grade will I get?
gold_answer: Yes, if you drop and receive a WD grade between September 4 and September 17, 2026, the course continues to count toward your enrollment status for financial aid (Federal Pell Grant, FSEOG, Federal Direct Loan and NYS TAP). For example, starting with 12 credits and dropping a 3-credit course on September 17, you remain full-time. However, your NYS TAP award may be prorated and you may use the equivalent of 6 TAP points for that term. The grade is WD: a non-punitive grade for a class dropped via CUNYfirst after the financial aid certification date but before the published withdrawal period. The course and grade will not appear on transcripts, and if you never attended, a WN replaces it.

question: What do I need to be considered for the clinical Dental Hygiene program?
gold_answer: Complete the six required prerequisite courses: ENG 1101 (or ENG 1101CO or ENG 1101ML), a Mathematical and Quantitative Reasoning course (3-4 credits), SOC 1101, BIO 2311, BIO 2312, and CHEM 1000 or higher. You are considered for the clinical program during the Fall semester if you are CUNY proficient in writing and math and proficient at or above the 12th grade level in reading, and have completed the 21 or 22 required general education credits with at least a C in biology and chemistry and a minimum combined average of 2.5. Seats are allocated by highest cumulative average, so completing the introductory courses does not guarantee progression; the average GPA for acceptance has been approximately 3.4 or higher. The introductory courses must be completed within four semesters, or you are required to transfer out of the dental hygiene curriculum.

question: I'm a transfer student. How do my general education credits transfer, and what about writing intensive credit?
gold_answer: Under Pathways, courses passed for credit at any CUNY college transfer for credit at any other CUNY college, and Required Common Core, Flexible Common Core and College Option courses transfer in the same category. 'Gateway' courses transfer for major credit at CUNY colleges that offer the major. All Common Core and College Option requirements are waived for students with a prior baccalaureate degree. You can appeal the Pathways category of a transferred course with the Transfer Appeal Form (email transfercreditappeal@citytech.cuny.edu). Writing intensive (WI) courses completed at other CUNY colleges or colleges with articulation agreements count. Required WI courses depend on credits transferred: fewer than 30: 4 for the bachelor's, 2 for the associate; 30-59.9: 3 for the bachelor's, 1 for the associate; 60-89.9: 2 for the bachelor's, none for the associate; 90+: 1 for the bachelor's; prior baccalaureate degree: 0.

question: How do I submit a SAP appeal and what do I need to include?
gold_answer: Submit the appeal through ProVerifier+ at https://cuny.proed.org using your CUNY Login, via the link in your email notification or your CUNYfirst To Do List. You must be enrolled in the current semester. Include a personal statement explaining the circumstances that affected your academic performance (such as illness or injury, illness or death of a family member, loss of employment, family or personal hardship, changes in your academic program), how they affected your ability to meet SAP standards, the changes you have made to succeed, and any other pending college appeals. Also submit supporting documentation, such as medical documentation, death certificates, court or legal records, termination notices, or other third-party documentation.

gold_answer: Before DEN 2400 you need DEN 2300, DEN 2311, DEN 2315 and DEN 2318 (DEN 2413 is a corequisite, taken at the same time). DEN 1200, DEN 1217 and DEN 1218 each need DEN 1100, DEN 1112 and DEN 1114 (C or higher). DEN 1100 needs CUNY proficiency in reading, writing and mathematics plus department approval, and DEN 1112 needs the same proficiency (they are corequisites of each other); DEN 1114 is for dental hygiene students only.

question: What do I need to take before Calculus III (MAT 2675)?
gold_answer: MAT 2675 (Calculus III) requires MAT 1575 (Calculus II) and MAT 2580 (Introduction to Linear Algebra). MAT 2580 requires MAT 1475 (Calculus I). MAT 1575's catalog text reads 'PREREQUISITE OF MAT 1475, MUST NOT HAVE PASSED MAT 2675', so its prerequisite is MAT 1475 and MAT 2675 is an exclusion, not a prerequisite. MAT 1475 requires MAT 1375 (Precalculus) or meeting the math placement for MAT 1475. MAT 1375 requires MAT 1275 (or MAT 1275CO) or meeting the math placement for MAT 1375. MAT 1275 requires CUNY proficiency in mathematics plus the listed high school GPA or Regents score criteria.
